text: In this month thirty-six of us said "the debt ceiling," the phrase Tom McClintock first put on the record in 2011, and it peaked on 2014-02-11. Then the count moved. Mike Kelly first said "the stop targeting of political beliefs" on 2014-02-11, and by 2014-02-26 the language spread: thirty of us said "political beliefs by the irs act," twenty-nine of us said "stop targeting of political beliefs by," twenty-nine said "targeting of political beliefs by the," twenty-nine said "of political beliefs by the irs." Twenty-five of us said "the stop targeting." Twenty-four of us said "the stop targeting of political beliefs." Twenty-five of us said "congressional budget office," which had first appeared in 2013. We converged on the same clause in the same window. This is what the record shows we repeated, and how many of us repeated it.
